To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the repertoire of IgM memory B cells changes with age, and that the different IgM memory populations have different repertoires, which may reflect their different roles in the immune system.

there are several populations of IgM memory B cells in the human periphery that are defined by CD27, IgD and IgM expression, that these different populations have distinct Ig repertoires, that the relative proportion of these populations change in the elderly, and that the relative proportion and repertoire changes may contribute to the age‐related decline in T‐independant responses.

1) the IgM+ B cells in the blood are not homogeneous and can be divided into multiple subsets, 2) some of these subsets are more common in older individuals, 3) the different subsets have different Ig gene repertoires, which is likely indicative of different immune responses, and 4) the level of Ig expression on IgM+ B lymphocytes is a useful marker of the different types of IgM+ B‐cell subsets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the age‐related aspects of IgM+ B‐cell heterogeneity, and the potential implications for the immune response to pneumococcal infections in the elderly.
the heterogeneity of human IgM B cells and the age‐related changes that may be responsible for the reduced immune responses in older adults.
the heterogeneity of human IgM memory and the impact of age‐related change on the repertoire of IgM memory.

the IgM memory compartment is heterogeneous, and the different subtypes have different characteristics.
there is no single “IgM memory” population, but rather a number of different IgM populations that are differentially affected by age.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

IgM+ memory B cells are a heterogeneous population, and that the changes in the repertoire and the relative proportions of different subsets of IgM memory may contribute to the increased susceptibility of the elderly to bacterial pathogens.

there is a lot of heterogeneity in IgM memory cells that has not been appreciated before and that the age effects on IgM memory cells are more complicated than previously thought.
